solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wild beast climbing up, ascending in the morning

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word up is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ascending likewise turns the morning abbreviation so it reads upward

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A wild animal scrambles uphill early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns UP into PU and 'ascending' turns AM into MA, both read upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The cougar or mountain lion is a wild cat famous for leaping and scaling trees and rocks.

clue.text: Countryman's game with short rod

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union, a ball game

indicators.note: short means the word for a rod loses its final letter

parts.note: a stick is a rod

explanation.surface: A country fellow plays a sport using a cut-down rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims STICK to STIC. The definition is 'Countryman's', read as 'Countryman is', so the 's is part of the definition rather than a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic is a rural person, a peasant or countryman.

clue.text: Pirate's short card game

definitions.meaning: to pirate is to copy unlawfully, to plagiarise or copy another's work
a shortened name for cribbage, a card game scored on a pegboard

explanation.definitionFit: To crib is to copy dishonestly, as a pirate copies; and it is the clipped name of cribbage.

clue.text: Choose not to join in, being top maybe

indicators.note: maybe says the word top is only one possible order of its letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the setter's playful reading: the letters of top are there being out, that is out of place

explanation.surface: Declining to take part, perhaps because you are already the best.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse-style trick: the answer read as wordplay says OPT is TOP 'out', disordered; 'being' and 'maybe' gesture at that state rather than giving the letters cleanly.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to choose not to participate in a scheme or activity.

clue.text: Sailor has all the cards, enough of them for one to play with

parts.note: a deck is a full pack of playing cards

parts.words: enough of them for one to play with
parts.note: a hand is the set of cards dealt to one player

explanation.surface: A sailor holds the whole pack, with enough cards for a single game.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckhand is a sailor who works on the deck of a ship.

clue.text: I make journey on track that's shimmery

parts.note: taken as written
to ride is to make a journey on horseback or by vehicle
a scent is a trail or track followed by hounds

explanation.surface: Someone travels along a railway line that shines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'track' looks like a railway but is the trail a hound follows by smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iridescent shows shifting rainbow colours, shimmering as the light changes.

clue.text: Copper has trouble with something useless — a climbing plant

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
cumber is an old word for a hindrance, a useless burden that troubles

explanation.surface: A policeman struggles with worthless rubbish and a creeping vine.
explanation.walkthrough: CUMBER, as in encumber, is a hindrance or burden.
explanation.definitionFit: The cucumber is a trailing, tendril-bearing vine grown up supports in gardens.

clue.text: Run after beer's started — this being weak?

indicators.note: after puts the run piece behind the letter from beer
the start of a word is its first letter, so only the first of beer is used

parts.note: a ladder is a run in tights or stockings

explanation.surface: After the beer starts flowing, you have to run, perhaps because of weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: A run in tights is a LADDER in British English. The definition is a playful hint: a weak organ sends drinkers running after beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak bladder is the familiar complaint, so the organ is described by its typical weakness.

clue.text: US author having effort to produce something that isn't prosy

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
a try is an attempt or effort

explanation.surface: An American writer makes an attempt at something not in prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is the opposite of prose, so writing that isn't prose is verse.

clue.text: Gown of fellow given cheers outside university

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: outside puts the word for thanks around the letter for university

parts.note: ta and cheers are both British informal thanks

explanation.surface: A man in a dress is toasted by people outside a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' links MAN to the rest. 'Cheers' and TA are both British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantua was a loose gown worn by women in the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: Obstruction ordered with security device to be brought in

indicators.note: to be brought in means the security device piece is placed inside the word for ordered

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, ordered
a lock secures a door

explanation.surface: Someone orders a padlock fitted to keep people out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like an anagram signal but is BADE, the past of bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A blockade is a barrier or siege preventing passage in or out.

clue.text: Hypocritical grief from snappy types trying to appear wet?

definitions.meaning: insincere sorrow put on for show

definitions.text: snappy types trying to appear wet?
definitions.meaning: reptiles with snapping jaws said to weep while devouring their prey

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means false, insincere sorrow, after the legend that the reptiles weep as they eat.

clue.text: One wearing authentic fur? That could be accomplished

indicators.note: wearing means the authentic fur goes around the single letter for one, as clothing around a body

parts.note: real means authentic
sable is a valuable fur
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A person dressed in genuine fur, a dream that might come true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts I inside REALSABLE, between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something realisable can be made real, achieved or brought about.

clue.text: Seaweed in a basin

definitions.meaning: an edible red marine alga, used in Welsh laverbread
an old word for a washing bowl, as in the biblical bronze vessel

explanation.definitionFit: Laver is both an edible seaweed and an archaic word for a washbasin.

clue.text: A family of trees? China has millions

parts.note: in rhyming slang china plate means mate, a pal
M stands for million

explanation.surface: Asking whether a group of trees is found in vast numbers in China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, so China means PAL. 'has' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Palms are a botanical family of trees and shrubs, the Arecaceae.

clue.text: It sounds like there could be two maidens here given a new look

indicators.note: the clue openly says what follows is heard rather than spelt

parts.words: there could be two maidens here
parts.note: a maid is a maiden, and an over in cricket with no runs is a maiden over, so maid plus over gives two maidens

explanation.surface: A place that might hold two young women has been redecorated.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over in which no runs are scored is a maiden, so MAID and OVER can both be maidens.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made over has been transformed or restyled with a makeover.

clue.text: Bolt from drive, terrified

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone bolts in fear from a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' suggests running away, but it is the metal fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivet is a metal pin or bolt for fastening plates together.

clue.text: Books about Military Intelligence for soldiers

indicators.note: about means the word for books goes around the intelligence letters

parts.note: tomes are large books

explanation.surface: Volumes on army spying written for the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is the British nickname for a private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommies is the traditional slang name for British private soldiers.

clue.text: Performer frowning in the auditorium?

indicators.note: in the auditorium is where things are heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: dour means stern and frowning

explanation.surface: A stage artist scowls at the audience in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A doer is someone who performs or carries out actions.

clue.text: Incendiarism — it could be thoughtless and chaotic

indicators.note: chaotic means the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Arson can be careless and disorderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' links the fodder to the definition; 'chaotic' shuffles INCENDIARISM and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiscriminate means done at random without careful judgement, unthinking.

clue.text: Last of birds on open country? Protection needed

indicators.note: last of signals that only the final letter of the bird word is taken

parts.note: a heath is open uncultivated land

explanation.surface: The final birds on the moor need shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places S above HEATH in this down entry; 'needed' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a protective cover for a blade.

clue.text: Worker in comfortable home finishing early for port

indicators.note: finishing early means the last letter is lost
in places the worker inside the home

parts.note: a nest is a cosy home
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords

explanation.surface: A labourer in a cosy house knocks off early to go to the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The ant is the crossword's stock worker; 'finishing early' cuts the last letter of the assembled word, not of the home alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantes is a port city in western France on the Loire.

clue.text: Our beast on the rampage, a wrecker

indicators.note: on the rampage means running wild, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Our animal runs riot, destroying things.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately wrecks or damages equipment.

clue.text: Garment of York turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: Ebor is the Latin-derived short name for York, from Eboracum

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing from York is turned upward.
explanation.walkthrough: EBOR, used for the Archbishop of York's signature and the Ebor horse race, reads ROBE turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long loose outer garment.

clue.text: Steer clear of dodgy region

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Avoid the shady area.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore is to disregard, to keep away from or take no notice of.

clue.text: Smell from bay caught drifting away

indicators.note: drifting away means the caught letter leaves the word for bay

parts.note: a creek is a small inlet or bay
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An odour comes from an inlet that was trapped and is floating off.
explanation.walkthrough: C for caught comes from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A reek is a strong, unpleasant smell.

clue.text: Part of hospital goes on after illness without interruption

indicators.note: goes on after means the hospital department follows the illness

parts.note: flu is a common illness
ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department

explanation.surface: A hospital department continues after an outbreak of sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluent speech flows smoothly without pauses or stumbling.

clue.text: Man of steel in plight rolling around in drink

indicators.note: in places the turned plight word inside the drink

parts.note: beer is a drink

indicators.note: rolling around means the plight word is turned backwards

parts.note: a mess is a plight or predicament

explanation.surface: A superhero in trouble staggers about in his beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of steel' suggests Superman, but it is Henry Bessemer, whose converter made steel cheaply; 'rolling around' sends the plight word backwards inside the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Bessemer invented the process for mass-producing steel from pig iron.
